topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Forces, Newton's laws and motion
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: Newton's Laws of Motion and Applying Forces; TGS 2026-27: Forces and Motion 2
topic.overview: Forces are interactions that can change velocity or shape. The resultant force, rather than one force considered alone, determines whether an object accelerates.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: A force is a push or pull caused by an interaction and is measured in newtons (N).
Force is a vector, so both size and direction matter.
The resultant is the single force with the same overall effect as all forces combined.
Balanced forces give zero resultant and therefore no acceleration: an object may be stationary or move at constant velocity.
An unbalanced resultant changes speed and/or direction.
Newton's first law states that velocity stays constant unless a resultant force acts; interaction pairs are equal and opposite but act on different objects.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: a push or pull caused by an interaction
the SI unit of force, symbol N
a quantity with magnitude and direction
one force representing the combined effect of all forces
the tendency of an object to resist a change in its motion
equal and opposite forces acting on different interacting objects

workedExamples.prompt: A 12 N force acts right and 7 N acts left. Find the resultant.
workedExamples.working: 12 - 7 = 5 N, in the direction of the larger force.

workedExamples.prompt: A runner travels 300 m in 50 s. Find average speed.

practicals.title: Force and motion comparison
practicals.aim: Investigate how changing a pulling force affects trolley motion.
practicals.variables: IV: applied force; DV: time, speed or acceleration proxy; controls: trolley mass, distance, surface and release method.
practicals.method: Use a trolley on the same track, vary force systematically, measure motion with light gates or a consistent timed distance, and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: A larger resultant force produces a larger change in motion for the same mass.
practicals.safety: Secure the runway, keep feet clear of falling masses and use an end stop.
practicals.evaluation: Use electronic timing, repeat, calculate means and check friction or a sloping track.

commonMistakes: Saying balanced forces mean there are no forces.
Assuming motion requires a forward resultant at constant speed.
Pairing action and reaction forces on the same object.
examTips: Draw one force arrow per interaction and label it.
Choose a positive direction before adding forces.
For force pairs, name both objects: force of A on B and force of B on A.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Force and motion comparison
practicals.aim: Investigate how changing a pulling force affects trolley motion.
practicals.variables: IV: applied force; DV: time, speed or acceleration proxy; controls: trolley mass, distance, surface and release method.
practicals.method: Use a trolley on the same track, vary force systematically, measure motion with light gates or a consistent timed distance, and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: A larger resultant force produces a larger change in motion for the same mass.
practicals.safety: Secure the runway, keep feet clear of falling masses and use an end stop.
practicals.evaluation: Use electronic timing, repeat, calculate means and check friction or a sloping track.
